observations: Two gas cylinders are shown in the foreground: one orange and one white.
The orange cylinder has a brass valve and a protective mesh shroud.
The white cylinder has a silver-colored valve and a damaged handle.
The cylinders are sitting on a concrete floor with other cylinders stacked in the background.
No weight markings or expiry dates are visible on the cylinders in the photos.

claims.evidence: The white cylinder shows significant wear and a damaged handle, which contradicts a 'neat' appearance.
The capacity stamp is not visible in the provided photos.

claims.claim: Recently tested and certified, no leak, the valve is new.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The cylinder may be expired or past its re-test date, making it unsafe.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturing or expiry date stamped on the cylinder.

risks.risk: The valve may be leaking or the cylinder may be empty.
risks.proof: A video showing a soap-bubble leak test on the valve and a weight reading.
risks.if_unproven: as empty and requiring a valve replacement

risks.risk: The cylinder may be a different capacity than claimed (e.g., 6.6kg).
risks.proof: A photo of the weight stamp on the handle or shroud.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the weight stamp (e.g., 12.5kg) on the cylinder.
Photo of the expiry or re-test date stamped on the cylinder.
Video of the valve being tested for leaks.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
